title: Marseille 1993: champions of Europe, and a bribe
checked: VA-OM 20 May 1993, 0-1, Boksic 21'; Eydelie the go-between for Tapie and Bernes; Robert and Burruchaga accepted, Glassmann refused and went public; 250,000 francs dug up in the garden of Robert's aunt (Wikipedia, The New World, WSC). Final 26 May 1993 Munich, Boli header 43' from Abedi Pele's corner (Wikipedia final, Afrik-Foot). Title stripped Sept 1993 (La Libre: 22 Sept), offered to PSG who refused, never awarded (Wikipedia x2, What a Howler); UEFA barred them from 1993-94 Champions League, Monaco took the place after PSG declined (Wikipedia, WSC); administrative relegation to Division 2 (La Libre: April 1994; Wikipedia). Tapie convicted, served six months (Wikipedia, The New World). Glassmann FIFA Fair Play award 1995 (Wikipedia, search reports). Table top 4 from Wikipedia 1992-93 D1 (2 pts a win). Four titles in a row 1989-92 and PSG's 2025 win as the next French champions of Europe: club honours. Marseille kept the Champions League (UEFA never removed it).

lines.text: Six days before Marseille became champions of Europe, their club bribed the opposition.
lines.say: Six days before Marsay became champions of Europe, their club bribed the opposition.

lines.text: Bernard Tapie's Marseille ruled France. Four league titles in a row, and a European final coming.
lines.say: Bernar Tappee's Marsay ruled France. Four league titles in a row, and a European final coming.

lines.text: Twentieth of May, 1993. A league game at Valenciennes. Milan in Munich, six days later.
lines.say: Twentieth of May, nineteen ninety-three. A league game at Valonsyen. Milan in Munich, six days later.

scene.title: Six days
scene.sub: 20 May: at Valenciennes · 26 May: Milan in Munich

lines.text: The plan: pay Valenciennes players to ease off, so Marseille stayed fresh for the final.
lines.say: The plan: pay Valonsyen players to ease off, so Marsay stayed fresh for the final.

lines.text: The go-between was Marseille midfielder Jean-Jacques Eydelie.
lines.say: The go-between was Marsay midfielder, Jon Jak Aydelee.

lines.text: Two Valenciennes players took it: Jorge Burruchaga and Christophe Robert. Jacques Glassmann said no.
lines.say: Two Valonsyen players took it: Horhay Booroochahga, and Kreestoff Robair. Jak Glassman said no.

lines.text: Marseille won one-nil. Then Glassmann went public.
lines.say: Marsay won one-nil. Then Glassman went public.

scene.note: Bokšić 21' · Glassmann tells the world he refused a bribe

lines.text: But first, Munich. Abedi Pelé's corner. Basile Boli's header. Marseille, champions of Europe.
lines.say: But first, Munich. Abedee Pelay's corner. Bazeel Bolee's header. Marsay, champions of Europe.

lines.text: Then the police dug up two hundred and fifty thousand francs, in the garden of Robert's aunt.
lines.say: Then the police dug up two hundred and fifty thousand francs, in the garden of Robair's aunt.

scene.headline: Bribe cash found buried in a garden
scene.standfirst: Investigators dig up 250,000 francs at the home of Valenciennes player Christophe Robert's aunt.

lines.text: In September, the federation stripped Marseille of the French title.
lines.say: In September, the federation stripped Marsay of the French title.

lines.text: Second-placed PSG were offered it, and said no. To this day, France has no champion for 1993.
lines.say: Second-placed P S G were offered it, and said no. To this day, France has no champion for nineteen ninety-three.

lines.text: UEFA banned them from defending their crown. In 1994, they were relegated.
lines.say: Yooayfah banned them from defending their crown. In nineteen ninety-four, they were relegated.

lines.text: Tapie was convicted, and went to prison. And Glassmann, the man who said no, won FIFA's Fair Play award.
lines.say: Tappee was convicted, and went to prison. And Glassman, the man who said no, won FIFA's Fair Play award.

items.label: FIFA Fair Play Award · Jacques Glassmann

lines.text: But Marseille kept the Champions League. For thirty-two years, the only French champions of Europe.
lines.say: But Marsay kept the Champions League. For thirty-two years, the only French champions of Europe.
